name: Catherine Malone
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Catherine Dorrance Malone is a great-granddaughter of John T. Dorrance, who invented Campbell's Soup in 1897.
Catherine and her sister, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Jr., inherited an 18% combined stake in The Campbell's Company when their mother, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Sr., died in June 2025.
While Catherine doesn't have a role at the company, Mary Alice Jr. replaced their mother on the company's board in July 2025.
Their cousin, Bennett Dorrance Jr., and their mother's cousin, Archbold van Beuren, are also billionaire directors of the company.
Catherine and her sister grew up on their mother's horse breeding farm in Coatesville, Pa. Catherine, who inherited the farm, also owns a dressage equestrian facility in Wellington, Florida.

name: Ahmed Afif Topbas
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Ahmet Afif Topbaş derives his fortune from BİM Birleşik Mağazalar, Turkey's largest discount supermarket chain.
Founded in 1995, BIM has more than 12,000 locations across Turkey, Morocco and Egypt.
His brother Mustafa Latif Topbaş, also a billionaire, is CEO and cofounder of the company.
Ahmet owns about 12% of BİM, which also has locations in Morocco with 687 stores there and in Egypt with 356 stores.
He owns about 12% of the company which has annual revenues exceeding $5 billion and offers a popular mobile telecom service under the brand name Bimcell.

name: Jane Goldman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Jane Goldman is America's only female billionaire running a real estate firm. She heads up Solil Management, which she owns with her three siblings.
The youngest daughter of Sol Goldman (d. 1987), once New York's biggest landlord, she oversees a portfolio that includes at least 400 properties.
Trophies include apartments on the Upper East Side and the block of land in Midtown Manhattan that includes the Olympic Tower and the Cartier Mansion.
The family also owns a 17% stake in the World Trade Center developments in lower Manhattan.
Her brother Allan is co-chair but has taken a back seat in recent years. Her sisters Amy and Diane Kemper are senior advisers.
forbes_facts: The New York City resident paid $31 million in 2015 for a Palm Beach estate originally owned by the Kennedys; she sold it for $70 million in June 2020.
The Goldman family name is all over Yale University, from the law library named after Jane's mother, Lilian, to a $10 million endowed professorship.

name: Shayne Coplan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Shayne Coplan is the founder and CEO of Polymarket, which is one of the world's largest prediction markets.
Coplan launched Polymarket in 2020 to facilitate bets on everything from sports results, political elections, entertainment awards and more.
In October 2025, billionaire Jeff Sprecher's global stock exchange operator Intercontinental Exchange invested $2 billion in Polymarket at a $9 billion valuation.
The deal made Coplan the world's youngest self-made billionaire at the age of 27, thanks to his estimated 11% stake in Polymarket.

An NYU dropout, Coplan had previously secured a number of other billionaire backers including Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia, Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin, Figma cofounder Dylan Field, Zynga cofounder Mark Pincus, Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick and hedge fund veteran Glenn Dubin.
Billionaire Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and Coinbase, cofounded and run by billionaire Brian Armstrong, are also investors in Polymarket.

name: Chang Pyung-soon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Chang Pyung-soon is chairman of Kyowon Group, one of the biggest educational companies in Korea, which he founded in 1985.
With education and training centers in bucolic settings throughout South Korea, Kyowon provides training programs to some 43,000 Kyowon staff members.
He has diversified and the company now has interests in educational travel programs, leisure activities, hotels and health foods.
forbes_facts: His Kyowon Group also provides "lifestyle" products, including water purifiers and Oriental herb-based cosmetics.
Chang started out as a salesman.

name: Tan Eng Kee
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2022-2024)
forbes_bio: Tan Eng Kee is cofounder and CEO of Malaysia-listed Greatech Technology, a maker of factory automation equipment.
He set up the company in 1997 with his school buddy, Khor Lean Heng, who's the company's COO.
Greatech's customers include EV makers, solar energy producers and semiconductor companies.
The company, which listed in 2019, has eight factories in Malaysia and a testing facility in the U.S., one of its biggest markets.
forbes_facts: At age 16, Tan worked part-time at a bakery after school hours to supplement his family's income.
Greatech was part of Forbes Asia's Best Under a Billion list in 2022 and 2023.

name: Zhu Jiangming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2013-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2022)
forbes_bio: Zhu Jiangming is the founder of Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology, a Chinese electric vehicle maker.
Earlier in his career, he co-founded Dahua Technology, a supplier of surveillance equipment.
From 2008 to 2010, Zhu worked at Motorola's branch Hangzhou, China.
Zhu received a bachelor's degree in electronic engineering from China's Zhejiang University in 1990.
